scientific_question: Does the released per-ID retirement rule exhibit a predictable multiplicity-by-evidence phase boundary rather than a single hand-picked 8-versus-4+4 example?

analytic_prediction.retirement_eligible_regime: For p_hat=0.90 and consistency=true, canonical k=1 retires iff N>=M. Under a balanced exact k-refinement, all k IDs retire iff N>=kM; hence representation-only class-decision divergence occurs for M<=N<kM.
analytic_prediction.non_retirement_regimes: For frozen p_hat=0.10 or 0.50 with the released default retirement predicates, neither canonical nor split should retire on this grid; the fragmentation boundary is specific to evidence that is otherwise retirement-eligible.
analytic_prediction.quotient_credit_prediction: Replacing per-ID attempt gating by class-level evidence aggregation collapses the boundary back to N>=M for every k.

derived_mechanism_quantity.name: representation-induced retirement lag
derived_mechanism_quantity.definition: minimum additional semantic feedback records required for the balanced native k-split semantic class to become fully retired relative to canonical

primary_endpoints: native semantic class active/inactive for every grid cell
future focal semantic sampling probability after the update/prune gate
pass_gate: All p_hat=0.90 native grid cells match the M<=N<kM analytic divergence rule; all p_hat=0.10/0.50 cells remain non-retired; quotient class-level prediction is N>=M independent of k; source commit/default threshold checks pass.
stop_gate: Any systematic released-function disagreement with the frozen analytic boundary stops the phase-mechanism claim and keeps P0 as a single deterministic counterexample only.
claim_boundary: Controller-level mechanism phase diagram for one released Skill-SP update/prune path; no endogenous task generation, no utility, no cross-system prevalence, no task-general behavior claim.
